question.problem:
Given that $f(x)=2x$, the derivative ${f}^{′}(x)$ can be computed using the definition of the derivative. The first few steps of this calculation are shown below:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={lim}_{h\to 0}\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h} \\  & ={lim}_{h\to 0}\frac{2(x+h)-2x}{h} \\  & =…\end{aligned}
$$

Finish the calculation, and hence find ${f}^{′}(x).$
question.worked_solution:
By proceeding with the remaining calculations we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={lim}_{h\to 0}\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h} \\  & ={lim}_{h\to 0}\frac{2(x+h)-2x}{h} \\  & ={lim}_{h\to 0}\frac{2x+2h-2x}{h} \\  & ={lim}_{h\to 0}\frac{2h}{h} \\  & ={lim}_{h\to 0}2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{′}(x)=2.$
